title: Iran Bars Women's National Football Team from Asian Games Despite Qualification
detail: Iran's Football Federation formally barred the Women's National Team from competing in the 2026 Asian Games despite the team having qualified. Officials cited 'lack of medal potential,' but sources reported the real reason was fear that athletes would seek asylum abroad — following the precedent set at the March 2026 AFC Women's Asian Cup in Australia, where five players sought humanitarian visas. During that tournament, other players refused to sing the national anthem in solidarity with Iranian protesters; state television labeled them 'wartime traitors.' The Asian Games ban represented the latest intersection of women's rights, sports governance, and the Islamic Republic's effort to maintain political control over Iranian citizens abroad. International sports bodies and human rights organizations condemned the decision.

media.caption: Iran women's team barred from Asian Games amid political tensions

title: US and Iran Near 'One-Page Memo' Framework to End War
detail: US and Iranian negotiators were reported to be 'getting close' to agreement on a one-page memorandum of understanding to formally end the US-Iran conflict. According to sources cited by Axios, the emerging framework discussed a 12-year halt on Iranian uranium enrichment, substantial sanctions relief, and reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to commercial traffic within 30 days. Trump had paused the US Navy's 'Project Freedom' escort operation on May 6, citing 'great progress' in negotiations. On May 7, Trump told reporters: 'We've had very good talks over the last 24 hours, and it's very possible that we'll make a deal.' The Carnegie Endowment and other analysts noted that Iran's nuclear question — including verification of its remaining enrichment capacity — remained the central unresolved sticking point in the emerging framework.

media.caption: US and Iran near framework deal to end conflict
